physical.weight-note: data sheet 11.1 lb at most; User Guide 12.1 lb with 48 serial ports and 11.8 lb with 48 USB ports

occupant-attrs.data-description: the memory card slot, which takes an SD or SDHC card

configs.description: The chassis with copper network ports, one AC inlet and no I/O modules. An illustration: no part number lists a chassis without I/O modules.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: The User Guide says the RJ11 modem port needs the optional internal modem card (56KINTMODEM-01). The jack is drawn on every build. No held document says whether the opening is present without the card.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the front with the modem card out, and its part number on the unit.

gaps.note: Figure 2-1 and the Quick Start Guide label an "Indicator LED" that no photograph held resolves. It is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the front, and a table of what its LED means.

gaps.note: The rear has three I/O module bays; no document gives a module a size. The three bays are declared at the positions and size of the windows read off Figure 2-2, each stating the class of module it takes, and no module is modelled or seated. The I/O Module Install Guide and User Guide Table 3-8 give the module types: a 16-port RJ45 module, a 16-port USB module, a 16-port Ethernet switch module and an 8-port RJ45 module for bay 1. Their rules are words only and no tool checks them: the 8-port module goes in bay 1 only, the switch module in bay 2 or 3, never bay 1, and the bays fill in order from bay 1.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of an I/O module, and a straight-on photograph of the rear.

gaps.note: The chassis also ships with two SFP ports in place of the two RJ45 network ports, with a dual AC inlet, or with dual DC inputs. No photograph of the DC inlet is held and none of the SFP rear at a usable size, so only the copper network and single AC build is drawn.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear of an SFP model and of a DC model.

gaps.note: The four faces draw the envelope only. The User Guide places the battery and modem door on the top and the product label on the underside, and the Quick Start Guide says the sides carry air vents. The angled photographs show a vent field on each side and the door at the right-hand rear of the top, but not at a size that gives a position, so none is drawn.
gaps.wanted: photographs of the lid, the underside and both flanks, with the ear brackets off.

console.note: User Guide, Table 3-4: "(1) RJ45-type 8-pin connector (DTE)", RS-232C, 9600 baud by default. The Quick Start Guide gives the pin assignments. The jack is the console jack, not an Ethernet jack.

ears.note: Data sheet: "Front-mid-rear mounting brackets". The Quick Start Guide and User Guide Figure 2-1 label the bracket "Front-mid-rear Mounting Bracket", and the figure shows it at the front of the body as shipped. No document gives a distance for any position, so none is written.

front.note: User Guide, Figure 2-1 and Chapter 2, "Front Console Panel Ports": the LCD and keypad, two USB type A host ports, one SD memory card slot, one RJ45 console port with an LED, and the RJ11 modem port. The Quick Start Guide hardware overview names the same parts and an indicator LED. The photograph shows the LCD to the left of the keypad, then the card slot, the two stacked USB ports, the console jack and the modem jack at the right-hand end. The logo is at the left-hand end. The card slot is the dark strip printed MEMORY CARD, left of the USB ports (Figures 2-1 and 2-13). Its position is read off the photograph, about 25.8 mm long, and the part is the full-size slot drawn for another maker's front, which reads 25.2 mm. Figure 2-13 shows it empty and the guide says the card is the user's own, so no card is drawn.

interface-names.note: Quick Start Guide, section 5: "Both of the SLC 8000 network ports (Ethernet 1 and Ethernet 2)". Section 2 says the system interface shows an SFP port as Ethernet 1 or Ethernet 2. The guide does not say which jack is which, so the upper jack is Ethernet 1, as the first jack it tells the user to connect.

layout-source.note: Every position on the front and rear is read off the photographs in the User Guide: Figure 2-1 for the front (580 px for the 438.15 mm body, 60 px for the 44.45 mm face, 1.32 px/mm across and 1.35 down) and Figure 2-2 for the rear (1157 px for the body across, 112 px for the face down, 2.64 px/mm across and 2.52 down). Both are small figures, so each position is estimated to within a few millimetres, and the logo, read off its outline in the figure, to within about 10 mm. The User Guide has no dimensioned drawing and no straight-on photograph.

modem.note: User Guide, Chapter 2: "One RJ11 modem port on the front panel". Use of it "requires installation of an optional modem card". The photograph shows the jack, and the word MODEM printed above it. The jack is drawn because the face carries it, and the gap `modem-card` says what is not known.

network.note: Data sheet: "2 GbE (10/100/1000BT) ports on RJ45 or 2 SFP Fiber/Copper port". User Guide, Table 3-4: "(2) 10/100/1000 Base-T RJ45 Ethernet with LED indicators". This model draws the copper variant. The quick start guide names the upper port as the one to connect.

power.note: Data sheet: "AC model input (single/dual): 100-240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz". User Guide, Table 3-4: "IEC 60320/C14". The photograph shows one inlet and one rocker switch. The sources give "Less than 30W" (data sheet) and "Less than 25W with 48 RS232 serial ports", "Less than 45W with 48 USB ports" (User Guide), which differ, so no chassis draw is recorded.

rear.note: User Guide, Figure 2-2 and Quick Start Guide section 1: dual network ports at the left, three I/O module bays named Bay 1, Bay 2 and Bay 3, and the power inlet at the right, with a rocker switch. "Bay 1 is the slot next to the Ethernet ports and Bay 3 is the slot beside the power supply module." The bays read about 112 mm wide in Figure 2-2. The three bays are declared at those positions, each stating the class of I/O module it takes; their positions and size are read off the photograph and are estimates. No module is modelled.

size.note: Lantronix SLC 8000 data sheet (MPB-00009 Rev O), Physical: "30.5 x 43.8 x 4.4 cm (12 x 17.25 x 1.75 in), 1U". The User Guide, Table 3-4, gives "1U, 1.75 in x 17.25 in x 12 in". The two agree. The width of 17.25 in is 438.15 mm, which is narrower than the 482.6 mm rack face, so it is taken as the body between the ears. The sources do not say so in words. The data sheet gives 11.1 lb at most and the User Guide gives 12.1 lb with 48 serial ports, so no weight is recorded.

usb.note: User Guide, Table 3-4: "(2) ports, type A, host USB 2.0". The ports are drawn with the white USB 2.0 tongue.
